task: What determines a standing-raising (RAISE / promotion) outcome? Coded only from SOURCES.md and TASK.md.

coding_conventions.target_type: The higher-standing home at stake for the item. If the item's own text names a home, that home is used. Otherwise, for R-36 items, the home of the review itself ('AI Architecture Promotion Review' -> AST-013 OPERATING_INSTRUCTIONS) is used, and the item is flagged in notes.
coding_conventions.evidence: Integer only if the text states an integer (or a number word) for this item. Ranges ('2–3'), approximations ('2-ish') and lists without a count are coded UNK. The stated form is kept in 'stated'.
coding_conventions.ground_for_promoted: PROMOTED items with ground UNK are eligible as P. Only a CHOICE ground excludes an item. See sensitivity S3 in EXECUTION.md.
coding_conventions.undetermined_pairs: A (P,Q) pair counts as UNDETERMINED only if an UNK field could make it falsifying. Pairs already non-falsifying on known values (a known parameter mismatch, or known evidence(Q) < evidence(P)) are left out of every list.
coding_conventions.verdict: FALSIFIED = at least one deciding pair. SURVIVES = no deciding pair and no undetermined pair. UNDETERMINED = no deciding pair, but at least one undetermined pair.
coding_conventions.actor_equality: Actors are compared as named strings; 'PO/ARB' is not equal to 'ARB'.
coding_conventions.R36_join: S5 (R-36 decisions) is joined to S4 (promotion matrix) by candidate name. S4 supplies the evidence counts; S5 supplies the outcomes and the actor. The join is an INFERENCE, supported by S5's category counts matching S4 exactly (see EXECUTION.md).

deciding_pairs.why: evidence(Q)=2 ≥ evidence(P)=2; M_E has no parameters. P = protocol adopted by the PA as operating standard; Q = the same protocol refused a standards document on the Phase 16 RULE.

M_A.note: The M_E deciding pair (E26,E27) is not a pair here: the actors differ (PA vs the session author). E27's actor has no PROMOTED counterpart.

M_T.note: (E26,E27) is not a pair here: the targets differ (OTHER vs STANDARD-DOC). (E01,E27) is critical: the text names at most 2 instances for E01, and if E01's evidence were coded 1 or 2, (E01,E27) would falsify M_T.

M_C.statement: Not needed on the determinate evidence: M_A, M_T and M_AT are each unfalsified. M_C cannot be ruled out, because each of them has undetermined pairs, and M_T would fall under either integer reading of E01's evidence. The one falsification (of M_E) comes from a RULE about authorization (Phase 16), not from an evidence threshold, so a non-evidence mechanism remains an open HYPOTHESIS.
